facts: Aquaculture is the farming of fish, shrimp, abalone, algae, and other seafood.
Farmers raise species such as catfish, salmon, and trout.
Aquaculture began in China a few thousand years ago.
Aquaculture supplies over 20% of all seafood harvested worldwide.
false_claims: Aquaculture means catching wild fish in the ocean.
notes: Reviewed: removed overlap and vague pronouns; paraphrased from wiki lead.

facts: An abbreviation is a shorter way to write a word or phrase.
People use abbreviations for words they write often.
Some abbreviations use an apostrophe, but many use periods instead.
Many English abbreviations come from Latin words.
The abbreviation i.e. stands for id est and means that is.
The abbreviation e.g. stands for exempli gratia and means for example.
The abbreviation et al. stands for et alii and means and others.
false_claims: i.e. means for example.
e.g. means that is.
notes: Reviewed: split Latin abbreviations into separate scorable facts (i.e./e.g./et al.).

facts: An Abrahamic religion is a religion whose followers honor the prophet Abraham.
Followers believe Abraham and his descendants play an important role in spiritual history.
The best-known Abrahamic religions are Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
Smaller traditions sometimes grouped with them include Samaritanism, Druze, Rastafari, and the Bahá'í Faith.
Mandaeism is usually not called Abrahamic because its followers reject Abraham as a prophet.
false_claims: All religions that mention Abraham are Abrahamic religions.
notes: Reviewed: softened wording; split long Mandaeism bullet.

facts: Anatomy is the study of the bodies of people and other animals, inside and out.
Anatomists study the position and structure of body parts such as bones, muscles, and organs.
A person who studies anatomy is called an anatomist.
Anatomy helps doctors and scientists understand how living bodies work.
false_claims: Anatomy only studies the outside of the body.
notes: Reviewed: merged redundant bullets; fixed imprecise organ examples; domain=body.

facts: An asteroid is a small rocky body that orbits the Sun in the inner solar system.
Asteroids are like planets but much smaller.
Most asteroids orbit in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
A few asteroids have smaller moons called asteroid moons.
false_claims: Asteroids are stars that orbit the Sun.
notes: Reviewed: deduplicated overlapping bullets; fixed grammar on asteroid moons.

facts: Angola, officially the Republic of Angola, is a country in southern Africa.
It borders Namibia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Zambia.
Its western border touches the Atlantic Ocean.
Angola is the seventh-largest country in Africa.
Luanda is the capital and largest city of Angola.
false_claims: Angola is a country in South America.
notes: Reviewed: removed duplicate Luanda bullet; domain=geography; shortened borders fact.

facts: A boot is footwear that protects the foot and ankle.
Boots are higher and larger than shoes and sandals.
Some boots are high enough to protect the calves as well.
Boots may be held on with laces or straps.
Many boots have a strong sole to protect the bottom of the foot.
notes: Reviewed: light paraphrase for story-coverability.

facts: In light, black is the absence of all color.
In painting, black pigment can be made by mixing other colors.
In heraldry, black is called sable.
Black is the opposite of white.
false_claims: Black is a color of light, like red or blue.
notes: Reviewed: removed vague pronouns; clarified painting fact.

facts: To chat is to talk about ordinary things that are not very important.
A person can chat with one other person or with a group.
Online chat lets many people send messages at the same time on the Internet.
People chat in chat rooms or messaging apps on phones and computers.
false_claims: Chat only happens face to face, never online.
notes: Reviewed: replaced dated messenger names; shortened long bullets; domain=everyday.

facts: Time Cube was a personal website created in 1997 by Otis Eugene Ray.
On the site, Ray described a theory he called Time Cube.
He claimed Earth has cubic symmetry and that time rotates through four corners.
He also claimed that modern physics is wrong.
Scientists rejected these ideas because they cannot be tested.
false_claims: Scientists confirmed Ray's Time Cube theory.
Time Cube is accepted modern physics.
notes: Reviewed: framed as Ray's claims vs. scientific rejection; domain=other; fixed grammar.

facts: The Census of Marine Life was a ten-year survey of ocean life that began in 2000.
Researchers from more than 70 countries contributed data to the project.
The project cost over one billion U.S. dollars.
Ron O'Dor of Dalhousie University in Canada led the effort.
notes: Reviewed: reordered for clearer narrative flow; light paraphrase.

facts: Maize, also called corn in some countries, is a cereal grain in the grass family.
People first grew maize in ancient Central America.
About 1 billion tonnes of maize are harvested every year.
Most maize is used for animal feed, ethanol, starch, and syrup rather than direct human food.
false_claims: Most maize is eaten directly by people as table corn.
notes: Reviewed: removed vague pronouns; consolidated usage facts.

facts: Dutton Speedwords is a made-up language written by Reginald John Garfield Dutton.
The idea of Dutton Speedwords is to make frequent words short, and very frequent words very short.
Dutton Speedwords can be used as a second language for international communications.
Dutton Speedwords is also a shorthand writing system – this means you can use it to write quickly.
notes: Reviewed: no substantive changes needed.

facts: Distance is how far one thing is from another thing.
Distance is also a measure of the space between two things.
Distance can be measured along any path.
Someone who walks in a circle travels a distance even if their ending position is unchanged.
notes: Reviewed: inclusive pronoun; removed vague opener on last fact.

facts: A diesel-electric engine is a diesel generator, a diesel engine that drives an electric generator.
The generator feeds electric power to an electric motor which turns a driveshaft.
Its efficiency is higher than when an engine drives a shaft through gears.
Most locomotives and many ships use diesel-electric drive.
false_claims: A diesel-electric engine burns fuel to turn wheels directly with no generator.
notes: Reviewed: added rater trap; facts unchanged.

facts: Et cetera means and the rest in Latin.
It is often used in English to shorten a longer list.
People usually write et cetera as etc.
Writing ect is incorrect because it does not abbreviate et cetera properly.
false_claims: Etc. is the symbol for the word and.
Ect. is a correct spelling of et cetera.
notes: Reviewed: removed incorrect symbol-for-and fact; added false_claims.

facts: An editor is a person who makes changes to documents or texts.
A newspaper or magazine editor prepares articles and may choose which ones to publish.
The lead editor of a publication is called the editor-in-chief.
Copy editors check spelling, grammar, and clarity before printing.
false_claims: An editor never changes the words in a document.
notes: Reviewed: removed disambiguation stub; fixed editor-in-chief typo.

facts: Financial capital is money and other assets used in business and trade.
It has value because people agree it can be exchanged for goods or services.
Money, stocks, and bonds are examples of financial capital.
Financial capital does not produce goods by itself; it represents stored value.
false_claims: Financial capital is the same thing as factory machines.
notes: Reviewed: domain=other; replaced oversimplified money bullet.

facts: A harbor is a sheltered place where ships can anchor safely.
Many harbors are also ports where ships load and unload cargo.
Ports have piers or quays where ships tie up.
Goods from ports move inland by road, rail, pipeline, or smaller river ships.
false_claims: A harbor is always far inland with no access to water.
notes: Reviewed: domain=geography; shortened and merged transport facts.

facts: The Island of Hawaiʻi is the largest Hawaiian island and the southernmost one.
The widest part of the island is 93 miles (150 km) across.
The Big Island has more than half of the land area of the State of Hawaii.
The island is part of the County of Hawaii.
false_claims: The Island of Hawaiʻi is the smallest Hawaiian island.
notes: Reviewed: fixed broken U.S. sentence split; grammar on State/County.

facts: Healing is a process by which the body repairs damaged tissue.
Cells work together to fix injuries over time.
Sometimes damaged tissue is replaced with healthy tissue of the same kind.
Sometimes damaged tissue is replaced with scar tissue instead.
false_claims: Healing means damaged tissue never changes.
notes: Reviewed: split colon-style bullet into two scorable facts.

facts: The International English Language Testing System (IELTS) measures English fluency.
Test takers choose the Academic Module or the General Training Module.
The Academic Module is for people applying to university.
The General Training Module is for work, training, or immigration.
false_claims: IELTS tests only mathematics skills.
notes: Reviewed: domain=other; consolidated redundant module facts.

facts: Ink is a liquid that is used to write, draw, print, or make marks.
Ink is used in pens, in some computer printers, and in printing presses.
In some countries, people write by using ink and brushes.
People usually write or print using black ink, but ink can be any color.
The first ink was used in Egypt about 2600 BC.
false_claims: Ink is a solid metal used only in factories.
notes: Reviewed: added rater trap; facts unchanged.

facts: The inch is a unit of length in the Imperial and U.S. customary systems.
Inches are written as in or with the double-prime symbol.
There are 12 inches in one foot.
One inch equals 2.54 centimeters.
false_claims: One foot equals 12 centimeters.
notes: Reviewed: clarified abbreviation wording after broken extraction.

facts: An insult is words that offend or hurt someone.
An insult may or may not be true.
Insults are a form of derogatory language.
Words like foolish or stupid insult a person's intelligence.
false_claims: An insult is always a true statement of fact.
notes: Reviewed: shortened long bullet; domain=everyday.
